summary: TB-EM-007 frontend E2E (Playwright, public URL) covering admin Schedule (day/week grid, nav, filters, legend, appointment panel, this-and-following edit/cancel, move a single visit so it becomes an exception, cancel with reason validation, book dialog filtered by assignments, repeat options, series clash list + skip), the child assign-therapist specialty filter, admin/guardian/therapist/supervisor Messages and permissions, guardian Family Home (visits, status pills, Time changed, attendance, reminders switch persists), forbidden states, mobile 390px (agenda/day grid/messages back/no overflow) and a browser in the Tokyo time zone showing center NY times correctly across the Nov 1 DST change. Found 1 HIGH bug and fixed it: the series clash list never showed in the UI. The cause was that lib/auth.ts call() dropped the error body, so ApiError.details was undefined and BookDialog could not read the conflicts. I retested after the fix and it passes. Also found 1 MEDIUM series bug and several minor UX issues.

minor.issue: The edit changes the series' own startTime (no split), so earlier visits (Oct 27–Nov 12, still 10:00) now report the series as 'Every week on Tue, Thu at 11:00'. GET series returns only the latest rule, so the summary is wrong for every visit before fromDate.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED BY TESTER: ApiError was thrown without the body as details, so e.details.conflicts was always undefined. book-clashes and book-skip-clashes never appeared and users could not book the rest of a clashing series. Now passes body as the 3rd arg. Retested: clash list shows 'Tue, Oct 27 — The therapist already has an appointment', and skip books 1 and shows '1 repeating visits booked, 1 skipped'.

series-edit-start is prefilled from series.startTime, not from the visit being opened. After one 'this and following' change, opening an earlier visit (Oct 27, 10:00) prefills 11:00. If the admin then changes only the length, all those visits would also move to 11:00 without the admin noticing. Prefill from zonedParts(appt.startsAt).time and the appointment's duration instead.
A visit cancelled on its own (Nov 10) shows 'this visit was changed on its own'. The wording suits a moved visit, not a cancelled one.

On the first render the dialog briefly shows the default tomorrow/09:00 (2026-10-22 09:00) before the effect fills in the visit's own date and time. Read immediately, the inputs give the wrong values.
Grammar: '1 repeating visits booked, 1 skipped because of clashes.'

issues: 45-minute blocks are shorter than 48px, so the therapist and the ↻ repeating marker never show on standard visits. The legend mentions ↻, but it is invisible on the grid (it is only in the aria-label).
Uses the browser's native date/time inputs rather than a styled picker (this matches the existing pattern).

'Coming up' is capped at 8 visits with no 'show more' (the 9th visit, Nov 19, is hidden). The guardian New conversation child option shows the legal name 'TEST_Alex Morgan' while threads show 'Alex Morgan'.

action_items: Keep the lib/auth.ts fix (ApiError details = body) or apply an equivalent fix.

Prefill series-edit start and length from the selected visit, not series.startTime. Consider splitting the series at fromDate (or storing the rule per segment) so the summary is correct for earlier visits.
Use different SeriesSummary wording for a visit cancelled on its own versus one that was moved.
Avoid the move-dialog first-render flash, e.g. initialise state from editing when opening.
Show the ↻ marker on short calendar blocks. Add 'show more' to the family Coming up list.
critical_code_review_comments: lib/auth.ts call() lost the error body (fixed). Any future UI that relies on structured 409 details depends on this.
AppointmentPanel: series-edit state is seeded from the series rule rather than the occurrence, which risks unintended time changes.
Messages/FamilyHome: there is no polling or refresh for new messages or the unread count, so a guardian must reload to see staff replies.
RepeatFields uses [...].sort() with no comparator. It is fine for 1–7, but a numeric comparator is safer.
seed_data_creation: Changes to demo data: series 08563b1e now starts at 11:00 from Nov 17 (Nov 17 and Nov 19 are at 11:00); Nov 12 visit dbea734b moved to 1:00 PM (exception); Nov 10 visit b152e09f cancelled (reason 'TEST_ family travelling'); new series with one visit on Sat Oct 31 (2443abda, Room 'TEST_Room clash') created then cancelled; messages: replies on TEST_Running late thread, new threads 'TEST_ Room change next week' (staff) and 'TEST_ Parking question' (guardian, Attendance).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Today in the env is Oct 21 2026; Harbor TZ is America/New_York. Only one child (Alex 8ac02ca1...) and two therapists (Leila e8c2ed95 with speech+OT, Jordan 2362ffb8 with no specialties). The appointments API rejects ranges over ~60 days (422). Calendar slots under an existing appointment are covered by the appt button, so use book-appointment-button and fill the date for those. Reproduce the clash: series Tue+Sat from 2026-10-27 at 10:00, 2 visits. Outbox is /app/apps/api/.outbox.
rca of the issue: Clash list missing: BookDialog checks `e instanceof ApiError && Array.isArray(e.details?.conflicts)`. opsApi uses rest.send -> call() in lib/auth.ts, which built `new ApiError(status, msg)` without passing the parsed body. lib/api.ts apiFetch did pass it, so the two error paths were inconsistent. The API correctly returns 409 {message, conflicts:[{date, reason}]}. Fix: pass `body ?? undefined` as details. Verified in the UI.
